info.desc: Lust For Life is the second solo album by American musician Iggy Pop, released on August 29, 1977 by RCA Records. It was his second collaboration with David Bowie after The Idiot, released earlier in the year. The album achieved critical acclaim and became Pop's most commercially successful album to date; it also remains his only gold-certified release in the United Kingdom. The Lust For Life sessions took place soon after the completion of a concert tour in support of The Idiot, the tour ending on 16 April 1977. podcast.body: Also released in 1977, *Lust for Life* was a key album in establishing Iggy Pop's solo career, following his detox and relocation to Berlin with David Bowie. These two albums helped transition him from a "deranged man in rock" to a respected figure. "Iggy's solo career really got moving with two albums, the Idiot and Lust for Life, both released in 1977."

podcast.body: Before commencing work on his own next album, David Bowie found time to produce Iggy Pop's *Lust for Life*. This album was recorded at Hansa Studios, located just 500 meters from the Berlin Wall. "Bowie tuvo tiempo para producir el nuevo álbum Diggy Pop, los Far Light en el estudio Hansa, ubicado a tan solo 500 metros del muro de Berlín."

podcast.body: Shortly after *The Idiot*, Iggy Pop released a second solo album. This album utilized some recordings from the Berlin Trilogy period, with a significant portion recorded in Geneva, the United States, and Paris with David Bowie's continued help. It achieved considerable success and received very good reviews. "el segundo disco de Iguipop también tuvo bastante éxito, tuvo muy buenas críticas, fue un gran disco."

podcast.body: The title track features one of the "coolest rock beats ever recorded." The drum beat was inspired by the theme song of a German news program that Iggy Pop and David Bowie watched while trying to "straighten out their lives in Berlin." Bowie picked up on the theme and gave Iggy the idea for the beat. "Still one of the coolest rock beats ever recorded."
